correctness.rationale: The repaired result preserves the exact numbers, makes the recurrent labels explicit as prior-implied, and gives a simplified complete sweep. For the closed centered radius-four map M, F=R₅M and the translation commutes, hence F-periodicity of period p implies M^(19p)x=x. On the prime ring, any proper spatial period implies constancy. Nakar–Ron Theorem 1 then leaves only constant words or strongly stable alternating runs of length at least five. With 19 sites there cannot be four such runs, so the only nonconstant possibilities are the rotations of 1^k0^(19−k), 5≤k≤14. Each is fixed by M and travels under F with primitive period 19. Independently built M for all 524,288 masks from the centered sliding sum, directly checked all target states are M-fixed, iterated each input to its first target label, and compared every class total and entry row to the tables. In order by depth, the two columns are (2,190), (90744,161120), (142956,85272), (38798,1900), (3306,0); the basin totals are 137903 for each constant and 13376,18202,24947,34200,33516,33516,34200,24947,18202,13376 for increasing block length. Rotation invariance preserves first entry and orbit labels in the two frames. Had any mask failed to hit the target set by four, the sweep would have rejected it. In the original F frame the witness trajectory is 21391→401507→235520→1792→0; precisely the depth-four masks fail F²²x=F³x. A separate independent direct-offset census also agrees, and the Paley figures used for comparison match the inspected original baseline and stored checker output. No submitted script was executed.
residual_risks: Complete enumeration only for the labelled nineteen-site rule; no other-order cutoff or general basin formula follows. No formal verification or expert attestation is asserted.

value.rationale: The degree-matched Paley-19 baseline fixes a natural order and degree before computation. A recurrent-set theorem by itself does not say how often the waves are reached. The distinct census shows 248482 of 524288 masks reach waves under the ordered neighborhoods versus 7524 reaching any nonconsensus orbit under quadratic-residue neighborhoods, and gives the exact per-wave probabilities and the sharp distribution of entry times. This quantifies attraction and a finite transient bound that cannot be read from the already-covered list of recurrent configurations. It is not offered as a scaling law.
residual_risks: The comparison is for these two natural tournaments at one order; it does not isolate a universal graph statistic controlling majority attraction.
